name: Management Information Systems
description: The bridge degree: enough technology to build and evaluate systems, enough business to know which ones are worth building. ⚠⚠ 13 Florida public institutions award 735 credentials, 628 of them bachelor's. ⚠ It sits in the business school rather than the computing school, and that placement — not the syllabus — is what most distinguishes it from computer science.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠ WHAT MIS IS FOR, STATED PLAINLY. It trades peak technical depth for the ability to work between the technology and the people paying for it. The occupational data bears that out: computer systems analysts earn $105,850 against software developers' $135,980 — but computer and information systems MANAGERS earn $175,140 with 55,600 annual openings, and MIS is the degree most explicitly aimed at that transition. ⚠ If writing code is the point, computer science is the better degree; if deciding what gets built and why is the point, this is. ⚠⚠⚠ WATCH THE INTRODUCTORY COURSE NUMBER. Florida carries the same introduction to information systems management under TWO numbers — ISM3011 at 12 institutions and ISM4011 at 10 — and NO institution carries both. Both are upper division, so credit is not lost either way; the risk is that a transfer evaluator matching ISM3011 against ISM4011 sees a mismatch where there is none. ⚠ Send the syllabus, not the number. ⚠ Largest producers: USF 183, FAU 159, Florida State 148, and notably Seminole State College at 103 — a state college in the state's top four for this degree, which is unusual and worth knowing if you want a baccalaureate without a university. FGCU 71, FIU 34.

cips.note: Management Information Systems, General — 13 Florida public institutions and 735 credentials in 2023: 628 bachelor's, 80 master's, 27 certificates of twelve weeks to a year. University of South Florida 183, Florida Atlantic 159, Florida State 148, ⚠ Seminole State College 103, Florida Gulf Coast 71, FIU 34.

related.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The comparison that matters, and it is about placement rather than content. Computer science sits in the computing school and aims at building; MIS sits in the business school and aims at deciding what to build. ⚠ Software developers earn $135,980 against computer systems analysts' $105,850 — but the management rung above both pays $175,140, and MIS is the degree pointed at it.

⚠⚠ The nearer neighbour on the operational side, and much more widely taught — 39 Florida institutions against this programme's 13. ⚠ IT is the infrastructure and support route; MIS is the analysis and management one. If you want to run systems, look there; if you want to specify them, look here.

⚠ A real overlap rather than a neighbour: ISM4323 Information Systems Security is carried by 10 Florida institutions and ISM4324 Cybersecurity Analytics by 6, so security is taught inside the MIS curriculum as well as on its own. ⚠⚠ The governance and risk side of security is closer to MIS than to computer science.

⚠ The parent field. An MIS degree is a business degree with a technology concentration, and the general business route with information systems coursework reaches many of the same jobs from more institutions.

⚠⚠ Where the analytical end of MIS has gone. ISM4545 Advanced Machine Learning for Business is already carried by 6 Florida institutions, inside the business prefix. ⚠ If the analytical work is the draw rather than the management, look at data science before committing to MIS.
